commit_message:
[RTL] Fix ICCM region lock bug and ICCM hash deadlock (#1417)

* unlock iccm region registers on hitless update

* fix iccm hash feature - ROM zeroizes ICCM and was triggering this early
the fix is to wait until the sha accelerator is unlocked (after KAT) before it starts hashing

* unlock the sha accelerator before triggering ICCM hash

* fix sha acc unlock to do it manually instead of relying on iccm hash trigger

* MICROSOFT AUTOMATED PIPELINE: Stamp 'user/dev/michnorris/iccm_reg_fix' with updated timestamp and hash after successful run

* Confirm ICCM writes while SHA ACC locked don't alter the hash
update SVA to use correct reset
update register model with hwclr on region locks

* add fence instruction to test to prevent race between iccm write and sha acc unlock for hash check

* MICROSOFT AUTOMATED PIPELINE: Stamp 'user/dev/michnorris/iccm_reg_fix' with updated timestamp and hash after successful run

commit_message:
[RTL] Enable RV Core DCLS feature and other FI countermeasures (#1293)

* [RTL] Enable VeeR EL2 DCLS and other FI features

Enable the dual core lockstep with a lockstep delay of 2 as well as
the following FI countermeasures:
- ICCM XOR address infection
- DCCM XOR address infection
- DCCM write readback
- Register file read output port comparison

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Upgrade VeeR EL2 core to commit chipsalliance/Cores-VeeR-EL2@60786de

Update the VeeR EL2 core with enabled DCLS feature as well as
additional FI hardening.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Add new VeeR rtl files to the file list

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Move config to common_defines.sv

The autogenerated defines for the VeeR EL2 core as are in .vh. Move
them to .sv to comply with the current flow in caliptra-rtl.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Intial DCLS integration into caliptra_top

Integrate the new DCLS feature into caliptra_top. For now
disable the corruption detection and do not connect the
tracer.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Connect DCLS error to CPTRA_HW_ERROR_FATAL

When the DCLS comparison detects a mismatch, raise a fatal error.

The soc_ifc_regs were re-generated using:
```
python3 tools/scripts/reg_gen.py \
  $CALIPTRA_ROOT/src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_reg.rdl
```

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Allow SW to enable or disable DCLS error

By writing to the new DCLS Control register, SW can disable or
enable the lockstep comparison error detection.

The soc_ifc_regs were auto-generated using:
```
python3 tools/scripts/reg_gen.py \
  $CALIPTRA_ROOT/src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_reg.rdl
```

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [VAL] Add test for enabling / disabling DCLS

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [VAL] Add DCLS error injection test

Test whether the expected alert fires when triggering the DCLS
error injection test input.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Use `caliptra_prim_buf` in VeeR EL2 core

Until now, we have used the generic prim_buf that is provided
with the VeeR EL2 core. Instead, we should use the prim_buf
provided by the caliptra-rtl repo as it correctly sets up the
synthesis barriers we need.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [VAL] Add ICCM and DCCM support to TB

As the VeeR EL2 core features RV_ICCM_ADDR_XOR and
RV_DCCM_ADDR_XOR are actived, the testbench needs to be adapted
to as well apply the XOR for the DCCM and ICCM backdoor accesses.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Capture MCU DCCM write readback error

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [DOC] Document the MCU FI features

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Add SW controllable mux for RV_CORE traces

As the main and the shadow core have debug traces, add
a SW controllable mux that enables switching between
the traces.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [VAL] Update coverage

Commit e9ebcae updated the RTL with the FSM protection
but did not update the coverage sampling and group. Fix
that.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Remove XOR ICCM address infection on ICCM measurement

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* [RTL] Set VeeR EL2 load_to_use_plus1 cfg to 1

Enable this option to optimize timing for the core.

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* update compile.yml and file lists

* port jtag idcode to parameter at caliptra core top level

* [RTL] Lint fixes for VeeR EL2 core

Signed-off-by: Pascal Nasahl <nasahlpa@lowrisc.org>

* fix elab error in uvmf_soc_ifc
fix lint errors in veer core

* Remove FW ability to disable DCLS corruption detection
DCLS corruption detection is enabled/disabled by a subsystem strap, always disabled in passive mode
Update dcls ctrl test to dcsl dis test - now confirms that dcls is properly disabled
Update dcls inject test to check for dcls corruption enable in hw config and inject error if so

* update docs to reflect dcls enable from subsystem
update dis test to inject an error and confirm it isn't logged

* update soc ifc reg cover/sample files after removing internal dcls register

* new register implementation in soc ifc uvmf bench

* add missing port to uvmf benches

+`else
+  parameter el2_mubi_t El2MuBiTrue = 1'b1;

commit_message:
[VAL] Gate MLDSA TB force/release on enable edges (#1412)

* [VAL] Gate MLDSA TB force/release on enable edges

The MLDSA stimulus injection blocks in caliptra_top_tb_services expand,
through their generate loops, to roughly 3000 always @(negedge clk)
blocks. Each one performed an unconditional hierarchical release on
every negedge, even on tests that never exercise MLDSA, which added up
to billions of no-op release operations per simulation.

Register the injection enables and release only on the deasserting
edge. A release on an object that was never forced is a no-op, so the
behavior is unchanged.

Measured on caliptra_top_tb with assertions enabled:
  smoke_test_ecc_keygen  924.0s -> 589.6s  (-36.2%)
  smoke_test_ecc_sign    835.0s -> 574.5s  (-31.2%)
  smoke_test_ecc_verify 1115.8s -> 736.3s  (-34.0%)

Simulation time is identical in every case and smoke_test_mldsa_kat,
which exercises these injection blocks, still passes.

commit_message:
[RTL] Clear KV write controls on zeroize (#1410)

* [RTL] Clear KV write controls on zeroize

A failed crypto operation never produces a result, so the KV write FSM
never starts and never clears KV_WR_CTRL.write_en via ~kv_*_ready. The
request stays armed and the next operation silently takes the KV path
with stale controls, zeroing the data that was expected.

Add zeroize to the hwclr term of the KV write control and write status
registers in HMAC, ECC and AES, matching the behavior already provided
to ABR by CALIPTRA_KV_WRITE_STATUS_ASSIGN in kv_macros.svh. The AES CLP
has no SW ZEROIZE register, so it uses debugUnlock_or_scan_mode_switch,
the zeroize source its KV clients already consume. SHA512 is not
affected: it has no key vault interface, and its KV client instances
are reused to drive the PCR vault.

Add three top-level assertions checking that write_en is deasserted
after zeroize.

Fixes https://github.com/chipsalliance/caliptra-rtl/issues/1159

* MICROSOFT AUTOMATED PIPELINE: Stamp 'user/mojtabab/kv-wr-ctrl-zeroize' with updated timestamp and hash after successful run

* Tighten zeroize KV write_en SVA guards to SW-write-priority case

decoded_reg_strb asserts on reads as well as writes, so guarding on it
alone also excused reads and swwe-blocked writes, leaving a verification
hole. Match the generated register priority exactly:
decoded_reg_strb && decoded_req_is_wr && swwe.

commit_message:
[UVM] Implement AHB (manager) agent (#1312)

* [ahb,dv] Define transaction items

* [ahb,dv] Define an interface to track an AHB bus

* [ahb,dv] Add a status item type

This can be used by the driver to report whether an has actually been
sent or was interrupted by a reset.

* [ahb,dv] A driver for the manager side of AHB transactions

* [ahb,dv] Define an AHB transfer sequence

This generates a single burst of reads or writes.

* [ahb,dv] Give a way to constrain wdata in ahb_transfer_seq

Extending constraints by writing a subclass is surprisingly tricky!
Hopefully, this will approach strike a sensible balance between
convenience and randomising things late enough.

As a "user", the commit adds ahb_single_write_seq, which is designed
to be easy to randomise when you want to "write 123 to address 456".

* [ahb,dv] Define a simple sequence item that holds a uvm_reg_op

* [ahb,dv] Define a simple reg adapter

* [ahb,dv] Implement layering virtual sequence

* [ahb,dv] Define an agent for the manager side of the interface

* [ahb,dv] Define ahb_single_read_seq

This is (marginally) easier to constrain to do a single bus read. But
it's very marginal: we just delete two lines from the layering vseq.

* [ahb,dv] Define a type for an AHB transaction

This will be used by the agent's monitor, which wants to pair up a
request and response.

* [ahb,dv] Define a monitor and add it to ahb_mgr_agent

* [ahb,dv] Extend ahb_mgr_reg_adapter to handle monitored bus items

This will now allow it to fill in uvm_reg_bus_op objects for items
monitored from the bus (which can be used to drive a
uvm_reg_predictor).

* [ahb,dv] Expose subordinate ranges from ahb_mgr_agent

This turns out to be handy if you have something that can see the
agent (probably a test that sees the agent through the environment)
and it wants to configure a sequence to know which address maps to
which subordinate.

[RDL] Fix memwidth in for message fifo in kmac_reg.rdl (#1330)

* [sha3ctrl,dv] Fix memwidth in for message fifo in kmac_reg.rdl

This block of address space is supposed to be 2048 bytes long, which
was expressed as 0x40 * 0x20. But the second number ("memwidth") is
measured in bits rather than bytes.

Rather than increase the memory width to something bigger than the
standard UVM bus width, multiply the number of entries by eight to
0x200 = 512, giving "512 32-bit word entries".

[RTL] Fix DMA response tracking and expand SoC IFC tests (#1369)

* [rtl] remove AXI access to AXI DMA block

* Clean up comments in soc_ifc_dma_reg_axs_invalid_test.yml

Removed stale comments for clarity in the AXI DMA test configuration.

* MICROSOFT AUTOMATED PIPELINE: Stamp 'ckuchta-dma-access' with updated timestamp and hash after successful run

* [TB] Add DMA transfer + SoC-AXI register-access stress/directed tests and coverage

Add reusable soc_ifc DMA verification that runs real AXI DMA transfers while
SoC-AXI concurrently accesses the DMA register block (which must be rejected),
plus functional coverage for those accesses.

Sequences/tests (verification_ip .../sequences/dma, tb/tests):
- soc_ifc_env_dma_sequence_base: reusable DMA transaction API (arm/status/FIFO
  push-pop/flush, transfer-and-verify, bounded AXI SRAM backdoor). Uses the RAL
  and axi_dma_reg_pkg route enums instead of hard-coded field offsets.
- soc_ifc_dma_xfer_item: constrained-random transfer descriptor (route/size/addr).
- soc_ifc_env_dma_reg_soc_access_sequence: drives SoC-AXI reads/writes to every
  DMA register (all rejected).
- soc_ifc_env_dma_xfer_stress_sequence + soc_ifc_dma_xfer_stress_test: randomized
  transfers with concurrent SoC-AXI register accesses.
- soc_ifc_env_dma_wr_fifo_directed_sequence + soc_ifc_dma_wr_fifo_directed_test:
  deterministic WR_FIFO/write_data transfer with continuous, fixed SoC-AXI writes
  to all DMA registers until the transfer completes.
- Register the new sequences in soc_ifc_env_pkg; remove the superseded
  soc_ifc_dma_reg_axs_invalid sequence/test.

Checkers/coverage:
- soc_ifc_predictor: predict SLVERR for SoC-AXI DMA-register accesses and add a
  passive, volatility-masked read-check of DMA registers (expected read data from
  the model for non-volatile fields only), matched by soc_ifc_scoreboard.
- soc_ifc_cov_if: add SoC-AXI DMA-register access coverage in axi_dma_cov_grp
  (register via RDL CLP_AXI_DMA_REG_* offsets + default drift bin, read/write) and
  cross it with the existing transaction-type coverpoints (disabled/WR_FIFO/
  RD_FIFO/AXI2AXI/MBOX2AXI/AXI2MBOX).

RTL/TB:
- soc_ifc_arb: add ERR_ARB_SOC_DMA_GNT assertion (SoC must never be granted DMA).
- hdl_top: back the DMA AXI manager port with a caliptra_axi_sram; compile.yml
  requires it.

Regression:
- Add the stress test to nightly_random and promote regressions; add the directed
  test to promote regression.

* [RTL] Restrict SoC-AXI SHA accelerator access to subsystem mode

RTL: gate SHA AXI usage to only in SS mode. Passive mode was allowing DMA AXI
user access to the SHA.

DV (soc_ifc / uvmf_soc_ifc):
- Add mode-aware SoC-AXI SHA access-control test (soc_ifc_env_sha_accel_sequence,
  soc_ifc_predictor, soc_ifc_sha_acc_axi_user_test) and uvmf_soc_ifc_ss target;
  requester AxUSER split 50/50 strap-vs-other in both modes.
- Add bound SVA (soc_ifc_sha_acc_state_sva) proving the SoC-AXI SHA route is only
  granted when authorized; add optional custom message arg to CALIPTRA_ASSERT.
- Add PCR-vault + ICCM-content-hash unlock in bringup so subsystem mode exercises
  a real SHA hash; capture global straps once at bringup into env configuration.
- Serialize concurrent SHA RAL frontdoor accesses (owner vs parallel hijack on the
  same AXI map) via a semaphore-guarded ral_read/ral_write to avoid a non-reentrant
  uvm_reg_map/adapter null-object race.
- Correct soc_ifc_axi_sha_acc_dis_tb to require SLVERR for passive AxUSER-0.

* Add soc_ifc sha test to regressions

* Apply suggestions from code review

* Make soc_ifc_dma_xfer_item.svh randomization safe from underflows and limit max_transfer size with pre-random check

* Remove randomized DMA test from promote pipeline

Removed comments related to assertion macros for clarity.

[rtl] - Deassert the AXI DMA write-request valid signal while all bits of the
four-bit pending-response counter are set. This prevents accepting a
sixteenth outstanding write and allows the counter to decrement when a
B response arrives before requests resume on the following cycle. Add
assertions and coverage for overflow, underflow, saturation, release, and
request resumption. Without this backpressure, delayed B responses can
wrap the counter to zero and make the DMA report completion while writes
are still outstanding.

[tb] - Expand the UVMF SoC IFC environment with configurable AXI SRAM and
recovery FIFO endpoints, response-delay injection, and reusable DMA
transfer support. Add long-transfer, response-pressure, and concurrent
SoC-access stress scenarios so the overflow condition and related DMA
behavior can be exercised at the block level.

-    // 2     RX Noise Filter
-    // 1     Rx Enable

-    //              --------------

commit_message:
[ENV] Add Nix devshells for dvsim + reg-gen; wire compile-to-core into fusesoc flow (#1338)

* [ENV] Add nix devshell for dvsim dependencies

Introduce a hermetic Python environment for the dvsim regression flow,
built with uv2nix and exposed as the flake's default devshell. Enter
it with `nix develop .#caliptra-dvsim` to get the pinned interpreter
and all Python dependencies needed to run tools/dvsim.

Motivated by the current mismatch between contributor and CI Python
environments, which has led to hard-to-reproduce failures when
locally-installed package versions drift from those actually used in
regression. Pinning via a lockfile plus Nix makes the toolchain
byte-for-byte reproducible across machines and removes any dependence
on the host distribution's Python or pip cache.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Add nix devshell for reg-gen tooling

Introduce a second uv2nix-backed Python environment, this time for the
RDL register-generation tooling (systemrdl-compiler and the peakrdl
exporters used to regenerate register RTL and UVM RAL models). It is
exposed as a separate devshell so contributors regenerating registers
do not need to pull in the heavier dvsim dependency tree. Enter it
with `nix develop .#caliptra-reg-gen`.

The dependency versions are pinned to those documented in the
top-level README and used by the current CI regeneration flows, so
that outputs produced from this shell match what CI produces and
tracked generated files stay stable across contributors.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Pin compile-to-core in caliptra-dvsim devshell

Add the compile-to-core generator as a Python dependency of the
caliptra-dvsim devshell, pinned via a Nix flake input tracking its
main branch, and relock so its console script is installed into the
shell's virtualenv and available on PATH.

This is a prerequisite for the following commit, which wires the
generator into dvsim's fusesoc invocation as a pre_build step. Pinning
via a flake input (rather than a released version on PyPI) is
deliberate for now: the tool is still evolving in lockstep with the
dvsim integration in this branch, so a mutable main-branch pin is the
lightest way to iterate on both sides without a release cycle. This
should be swapped for a proper version pin once the tool stabilises.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Integrate compile-to-core as fusesoc pre_build

Wire the compile-to-core generator into dvsim's fusesoc flow as a
pre_build_cmd. Before fusesoc runs, the generator converts Caliptra's
existing compile.yaml files into fusesoc .core files under a scratch
directory, which is then passed to fusesoc via an added --cores-root
alongside the project's src/ and tools/dv-classes/ trees. The
sv_flist_gen_opts block is restructured accordingly so fusesoc sees
all three roots at setup time.

This is needed because the majority of the build description lives in
the MSFT-format compile.yaml files, which fusesoc cannot consume
directly; generating .core shims on the fly lets the dvsim flow reuse
the existing source-of-truth without duplicating it. The scratch dir
is placed under the dvsim scratch path so it is scoped to a single
build and cleaned up with the rest of the build artefacts.

The generated .f/.scr filelist path template is also updated to
mirror the transformation fusesoc applies when naming its output
files (colons in the VLNV identifier become underscores), which is
otherwise undocumented behaviour and easy to trip over on rename.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] Exclude .lock files from the license header check script

These files are typically autogenerated by various build systems (e.g.
Cargo.lock, composer.lock, uv.lock, flake.lock) and as such do not need
a license header.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

* [ENV] dvsim build-scoped cores dir; git in .#caliptra-dvsim devshell

Changes address the Copilot review.

- tools/dvsim/fusesoc.hjson: generate the compile-to-core .core shims
  into {build_dir}/cores rather than {scratch_path}/cores, and point
  the matching --cores-root at the same location. {scratch_path} is
  shared across build modes, so concurrent builds could collide;
  {build_dir} scopes the shims per build, matching both the in-file
  comment and the commit that introduced them.

- flake.nix: make git available where it is needed.
  * commonShellHook runs `git rev-parse` to locate the repo root; it
    now references the binary directly via `${pkgs.lib.getExe pkgs.git}`
    so the hook resolves in both devshells without relying on git
    leaking in from the host.
  * The caliptra-dvsim shell additionally carries git as a package,
    because dvsim shells out to the git binary at runtime (branch and
    repo-root discovery in cli/run.py, plus GitPython in reporting).
    caliptra-reg-gen has no such dependency, so it is left out there.

Signed-off-by: Harry Callahan <hcallahan@lowrisc.org>

    not sure whether we'll be running lint tests in the same way for
    Caliptra, so it might make sense to decide this properly later on.

  - Similarly, remove the lint waivers from prim_util.

[dv] Copy prim_mubi_pkg from OpenTitan

The only manual change is to update the "auto-generated" header to
make it slightly more informative, and to remove the dependencies on
standard linter waiver files (since we aren't yet using that lint flow
in Caliptra).

[dv] Copy dv_base_reg from OpenTitan

This is almost a direct copy of hw/dv/sv/dv_base_reg, but the
dependency on lowrisc:prim:mubi has been changed to
lowrisc:prim:mubi_pkg (because we need to depend on the type, rather
than the RTL implementation).

This change is now a PR in OpenTitan as well (PR #30330)

[dv] Copy csr_utils from OpenTitan

[dv] Copy dv_base_agent from OpenTitan

This is the head of OpenTitan, plus PR #30337 (which avoids the core
having a dependency on a bus parameter package).

commit_message:
[RTL] Restrict SHA AXI Access in Passive Mode (#1357)

* [rtl] remove AXI access to AXI DMA block

* Clean up comments in soc_ifc_dma_reg_axs_invalid_test.yml

Removed stale comments for clarity in the AXI DMA test configuration.

* MICROSOFT AUTOMATED PIPELINE: Stamp 'ckuchta-dma-access' with updated timestamp and hash after successful run

* [TB] Add DMA transfer + SoC-AXI register-access stress/directed tests and coverage

Add reusable soc_ifc DMA verification that runs real AXI DMA transfers while
SoC-AXI concurrently accesses the DMA register block (which must be rejected),
plus functional coverage for those accesses.

Sequences/tests (verification_ip .../sequences/dma, tb/tests):
- soc_ifc_env_dma_sequence_base: reusable DMA transaction API (arm/status/FIFO
  push-pop/flush, transfer-and-verify, bounded AXI SRAM backdoor). Uses the RAL
  and axi_dma_reg_pkg route enums instead of hard-coded field offsets.
- soc_ifc_dma_xfer_item: constrained-random transfer descriptor (route/size/addr).
- soc_ifc_env_dma_reg_soc_access_sequence: drives SoC-AXI reads/writes to every
  DMA register (all rejected).
- soc_ifc_env_dma_xfer_stress_sequence + soc_ifc_dma_xfer_stress_test: randomized
  transfers with concurrent SoC-AXI register accesses.
- soc_ifc_env_dma_wr_fifo_directed_sequence + soc_ifc_dma_wr_fifo_directed_test:
  deterministic WR_FIFO/write_data transfer with continuous, fixed SoC-AXI writes
  to all DMA registers until the transfer completes.
- Register the new sequences in soc_ifc_env_pkg; remove the superseded
  soc_ifc_dma_reg_axs_invalid sequence/test.

Checkers/coverage:
- soc_ifc_predictor: predict SLVERR for SoC-AXI DMA-register accesses and add a
  passive, volatility-masked read-check of DMA registers (expected read data from
  the model for non-volatile fields only), matched by soc_ifc_scoreboard.
- soc_ifc_cov_if: add SoC-AXI DMA-register access coverage in axi_dma_cov_grp
  (register via RDL CLP_AXI_DMA_REG_* offsets + default drift bin, read/write) and
  cross it with the existing transaction-type coverpoints (disabled/WR_FIFO/
  RD_FIFO/AXI2AXI/MBOX2AXI/AXI2MBOX).

RTL/TB:
- soc_ifc_arb: add ERR_ARB_SOC_DMA_GNT assertion (SoC must never be granted DMA).
- hdl_top: back the DMA AXI manager port with a caliptra_axi_sram; compile.yml
  requires it.

Regression:
- Add the stress test to nightly_random and promote regressions; add the directed
  test to promote regression.

* [RTL] Restrict SoC-AXI SHA accelerator access to subsystem mode

RTL: gate SHA AXI usage to only in SS mode. Passive mode was allowing DMA AXI
user access to the SHA.

DV (soc_ifc / uvmf_soc_ifc):
- Add mode-aware SoC-AXI SHA access-control test (soc_ifc_env_sha_accel_sequence,
  soc_ifc_predictor, soc_ifc_sha_acc_axi_user_test) and uvmf_soc_ifc_ss target;
  requester AxUSER split 50/50 strap-vs-other in both modes.
- Add bound SVA (soc_ifc_sha_acc_state_sva) proving the SoC-AXI SHA route is only
  granted when authorized; add optional custom message arg to CALIPTRA_ASSERT.
- Add PCR-vault + ICCM-content-hash unlock in bringup so subsystem mode exercises
  a real SHA hash; capture global straps once at bringup into env configuration.
- Serialize concurrent SHA RAL frontdoor accesses (owner vs parallel hijack on the
  same AXI map) via a semaphore-guarded ral_read/ral_write to avoid a non-reentrant
  uvm_reg_map/adapter null-object race.
- Correct soc_ifc_axi_sha_acc_dis_tb to require SLVERR for passive AxUSER-0.

* Add soc_ifc sha test to regressions

* Apply suggestions from code review

* Make soc_ifc_dma_xfer_item.svh randomization safe from underflows and limit max_transfer size with pre-random check

* Remove randomized DMA test from promote pipeline

* [dv] improve parameter, path, and memeory access between dut and tb

* Split mem_backdoor classes into different files. Clean up some ofthe xfer_item creation

* Update .vf files

* Clean up DV methodologies in soc_ifc UVMF

* TB changes caught by code review

Removed comments related to assertion macros for clarity.

+`else
+    localparam bit SS_MODE = 1'b0;
+`endif

+    // A SoC-AXI SHA access is authorized only in subsystem mode with a matching
+    // AxUSER identity.
+    logic soc_sha_authorized;
+    always_comb soc_sha_authorized = SS_MODE & valid_sha_user;
+

+    // In passive mode soc_sha_authorized is always 0, so no SoC-AXI SHA access
+    // may be granted at all.

+        }
+    endgroup
+
+    `CALIPTRA_COVER(C_authorized_soc_request_reaches_sha,
+        sha_req_dv & sha_req_data.soc_req &
+        (sha_req_data.user == sha_dma_axi_user),
+        clk, !rst_b)
+`else
+    covergroup soc_sha_access_cg @(posedge clk iff (rst_b & soc_sha_addr));
+        cp_access_control: coverpoint {sha_user_match, soc_sha_gnt} {
+            bins matching_axuser_rejected    = {2'b10};
+            bins nonmatching_axuser_rejected = {2'b00};
+        }
+    endgroup
+`endif
+
+    soc_sha_access_cg soc_sha_access_cg_inst = new();
+

diff --git a/src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_arb.sv b/src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_arb.sv
index d0aa28b0..10262bf2 100644
--- a/src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_arb.sv
+++ b/src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_arb.sv
@@ -154,8 +154,13 @@ always_comb uc_sha_req = (uc_req_dv & (uc_req_data.addr inside {[SHA_REG_START_A
 always_comb soc_sha_req = (soc_req_dv & (soc_req_data.addr inside {[SHA_REG_START_ADDR:SHA_REG_END_ADDR]})) & valid_sha_user;
 
 // Requests to DMA
+// The AXI DMA register block is owned exclusively by Caliptra uC firmware (the
+// DMA assist is Caliptra's AXI manager, per the Caliptra Integration/Hardware
+// Specifications). SoC AXI agents are not permitted to reach it, so the SoC->DMA
+// path is held off here. SoC accesses to the DMA address range then fall through
+// to the unmapped-access term in soc_error below, returning SLVERR.
 always_comb uc_dma_req = (uc_req_dv & (uc_req_data.addr inside {[DMA_REG_START_ADDR:DMA_REG_END_ADDR]}));
-always_comb soc_dma_req = (soc_req_dv & (soc_req_data.addr inside {[DMA_REG_START_ADDR:DMA_REG_END_ADDR]}));
+always_comb soc_dma_req = 1'b0;
 
 //Check if SoC request is coming from a valid user
 //There are 5 valid user registers, check if user attribute matches any of them
@@ -256,4 +261,10 @@ always_comb soc_error = (soc_mbox_gnt & mbox_error) |
 `CALIPTRA_ASSERT_MUTEX(ERR_ARB_DMA_ACCESS_MUTEX , {uc_dma_gnt,soc_dma_gnt}, clk, !rst_b)
 `CALIPTRA_ASSERT_MUTEX(ERR_ARB_MBOX_REG_AND_DIR_ACCESS_MUTEX, {mbox_req_dv,mbox_dir_req_dv}, clk, !rst_b)
 
+// The AXI DMA register block is Caliptra-uC-only (owned over AHB); no SoC-AXI
+// agent may reach it. The SoC->DMA path is held off (soc_dma_req=1'b0), so the
+// DMA client must never be granted to the SoC. This guards against any future
+// re-introduction of a SoC->DMA path, independent of DMA state.
+`CALIPTRA_ASSERT_NEVER(ERR_ARB_SOC_DMA_GNT, soc_dma_gnt, clk, !rst_b)
+
 endmodule

[ERRATA FIX] Fix the spurious ECC error on DMA write to mailbox (#1352)

* change caliptra_sram model to return X data when not in active read

* Fix logic in mailbox to avoid rdata ECC check during a DMA dir-write to mailbox

* Add vcs logfile generation and manually build the ml-kem/tv directory

* Add a directed testcase to exercise the ecc-error on mbox-write-via-dma failing path

* Additional fixes to add robustness on mbox SRAM read and ecc calculations, with assertion and test case to verify

* Add fsdb-waves options for VCS sims

* latest rendition of mbox_protocol_race_ecc test (could not trigger the suspected error case)

* reduce header comments in files

* Remove protocol race test

Test breaks the MBOX protocol

* [rtl] add activity monitor to cg and soc_ifc

Since MBOX can be accessess while UC is idel when the SOC causes the
MBOX to transition states we need to ensure CG does not happen until
MBOX is complete with it's transition. There were Xs propagating through the
ECC check with the new design. Typically for other IPs within CLP the
UC has to be awake which forces the clocks to be active.

* Change active to busy to match crypto blocks

* MICROSOFT AUTOMATED PIPELINE: Stamp 'cwhitehead-mbox-sram-ecc-check-fix' with updated timestamp and hash after successful run

commit_message:
[dvsim] Add initial dvsim support files to tools/dvsim/ (#1331)

* [dvsim] Add initial dvsim support files to tools/dvsim/

This change lays down the initial scaffolding required to drive Caliptra
simulations with the lowRISC/OpenTitan dvsim tool. It introduces a tools/dvsim/
directory containing project-wide hjson configs, tool-specific hjson configs for
VCS/Xcelium/Questa, common coverage/xprop/UNR directive files, TCL helpers for
waves and coverage merging, a build/run Makefile, and a starter set of reusable
testplans. No DUT-specific *_sim_cfg.hjson files are added yet — this commit is
only the shared substrate that per-block sim configs will import_cfgs from.

What's added

Common project-wide hjson configs (imported by all sim cfgs)

- common_project_cfg.hjson — Project-level defaults consumed by
every *_sim_cfg.hjson: scratch_base_path/scratch_path layout, empty
build_pass_patterns / build_fail_patterns placeholders, exports for SCRATCH_PATH
and proj_root, and empty results-server hooks. Project/repo/doc/results-server
URLs are stubbed as empty strings for a downstream project to fill in.
- common_sim_cfg.hjson — The shared simulation flow definition. Sets flow: sim,
points flow_makefile at sim.mk, chains import_cfgs (common_project_cfg →
common_modes → fusesoc → {tool}.hjson), defines default build_dir / run_dir
layout, default UVM run_pass_patterns / run_fail_patterns, UVM verbosity
expansion table, default build_opts (UVM defines, SIMULATION,
DUT_HIER={dut_instance}), the default sim_tops/dut_instance scheme, canned
regressions (smoke, all, all_once, nightly), and per-tool coverage cfg file
pointers (VCS + Xcelium) so that individual DUT configs pick these up for free.
- common_modes.hjson — Reusable "sim modes" that layer on top of build_modes:
gui, gui_debug, waves, waves_off, cov (also injects +en_cov=1), profile, xprop,
loopdetect, build_seed (wraps +define+BUILD_SEED={seed} for reproducible
randomized builds), and a uvm_trace run mode. All are is_sim_mode: 1 so they
compose additively with each tool's build modes.
- fusesoc.hjson — Glue between dvsim and FuseSoC as the SV file-list generator:
sv_flist_gen_cmd: fusesoc, canonical sv_flist_gen_opts
(run --target=sim --setup --work-root=…), fusesoc_cores_root_dirs rooted at
{proj_root}/hw, and the .scr file dvsim will consume.

Tool-specific hjson configs

- vcs.hjson (366 lines) — Full VCS provider: SIMV/vlogan/vhdlan invocations,
+defines, wave/GUI/coverage/xprop/profile/UNR/loopdetect build modes,
coverage-related knobs (-cm, -cm_hier, exclusions), and hook-ins to the shared
vcs_*_cfg_file variables from common_sim_cfg.hjson.
- xcelium.hjson (269 lines) — Xcelium equivalent: xrun-based build/run commands,
wave/GUI/coverage/xprop/profile build modes, cov merge/report scripts, and paths
to Xcelium .ccf/tcl files under tools/xcelium/.
- questa.hjson (115 lines) — Questa provider (vlog/vopt/vsim invocations plus
wave/GUI/coverage build modes).

Build/run Makefile

- sim.mk — The flow_makefile dispatched to by dvsim. Provides build / run phases
with pre_build / post_build / pre_run / post_run hooks and glues in
sw_build_cmd, coverage-related targets, and (per tool) the compile + elaborate +
simulate steps.

Coverage / xprop / UNR directive files (per tool)

Under tools/dvsim/tools/vcs/:
- cover.cfg, cover_reg_top.cfg — hierarchical cov selection templates
- common_cov_excl.cfg — shared coverage exclusions
- fsm_reset_cov.cfg — FSM reset-state cov control
- unr.cfg — unreachable-analysis config
- xprop.cfg — X-propagation config

Under tools/dvsim/tools/xcelium/:
- common.ccf, cover.ccf, cover_reg_top.ccf, cover_reg_top_toggle_excl — coverage
config
- common_cov_excl.tcl, cov_merge.tcl, cov_report.tcl — coverage flow TCL
- unr.cfg — unreachable-analysis config

Shared TCL helpers

Under tools/dvsim/tools/:
- common.tcl — Shared TCL utility procs sourced by both simulators.
- sim.tcl — Simulator-agnostic driver TCL.
- waves.tcl — Wave-dumping directives (FSDB/SHM/etc.) invoked in waves mode.
- questa/sim.tcl — Questa-specific overrides for the simulate step.

+{

+      name: csr_hw_reset
+      desc: '''
+            Verify the reset values as indicated in the RAL specification.
+            - Write all CSRs with a random value.
+            - Apply reset to the DUT as well as the RAL model.
+            - Read each CSR and compare it against the reset value.

+    }
+    {
+      name: csr_rw
+      desc: '''
+            Verify accessibility of CSRs as indicated in the RAL specification.
+            - Loop through each CSR to write it with a random value.
+            - Read the CSR back and check for correctness while adhering to its
+              access policies.
+            - It is mandatory to run this test for all available interfaces the
+              CSRs are accessible from.
+            - Shuffle the list of CSRs first to remove the effect of ordering.
+            '''
+      stage: V1
+      tests: ["{name}{intf}_csr_rw"]
+    }
+    {
+      name: csr_bit_bash
+      desc: '''
+            Verify no aliasing within individual bits of a CSR.
+            - Walk a 1 through each CSR by flipping 1 bit at a time.
+            - Read the CSR back and check for correctness while adhering to its
+              access policies.
+            - This verify that writing a specific bit within the CSR did not affect
+              any of the other bits.
+            - It is mandatory to run this test for all available interfaces the
+              CSRs are accessible from.
+            - Shuffle the list of CSRs first to remove the effect of ordering.
+            '''
+      stage: V1
+      tests: ["{name}{intf}_csr_bit_bash"]
+    }
+    {
+      name: csr_aliasing
+      desc: '''
+            Verify no aliasing within the CSR address space.
+            - Loop through each CSR to write it with a random value
+            - Shuffle and read ALL CSRs back.
+            - All CSRs except for the one that was written in this iteration should
+              read back the previous value.
+            - The CSR that was written in this iteration is checked for correctness
+              while adhering to its access policies.
+            - It is mandatory to run this test for all available interfaces the
+              CSRs are accessible from.
+            - Shuffle the list of CSRs first to remove the effect of ordering.

+            - Randomly issue reset and then use hw_reset sequence to check all CSRs

+            - It is mandatory to run this test for all available interfaces the

commit_message:
[RTL] HW controlled ICCM content hash (#1292)

* first cut of ICCM hash feature
allows firmware to enable iccm mode in the sha accelerator which snoops the iccm write bus and calculates a hash of the data written to the iccm
currently stashing that hash in PCR4 which is blocked from being written any other way

Future fix: stash the hash in a local register and use it to extend PCR 4 and PCR 5 as current and journey registers

* Modified ICCM hash block to compute the hash of ICCM and store for extensions
FSM now extends PCR4 from it's reset 0s value as well as PCR5 as a journey register
Routed PV read port for sha accelerator to use for extension of PCR 4 and 5
Added PCR5 to the protected PCRs in the pcr vault so that FW can't modify them
Updated smoke test and directed test expected values based on hash extension being performed
Added sanity check for endianness by having FW compute a hash extend using the same digest and compare with the sha accelerator hw version

Documented the feature in the hardware spec
Added a section to the test plan for this feature

* lint fix for loop iterator going out of bounds

* Removed some intermediate signals and passed directly between modules.
Updated unit level benches with missing ports

* [VAL] ICCM write hash measurement: add 7 directed tests + shared library

Implements the "Coverage Gaps" table in docs/CaliptraPreReleaseTestPlan.md
(ICCM Write Hash Measurement section, PR #1292):

  directed_test_iccm_pcr5_journey      PCR5 Journey chains across 3 boots
  directed_test_iccm_fw_write_block    FW AHB writes blocked on PCR4 / PCR5
  directed_test_iccm_sha_ctrl_block    sha512_ctrl pv_write[0] blocked from PCR4 / PCR5
  directed_test_iccm_clear_hatch       PCR_CTRL[4,5].clear works, FW still cannot tamper after
  directed_test_iccm_mode_write_once   MODE.ICCM_MODE cannot be re-armed after completion
  directed_test_iccm_sha_acc_reuse     SHA acc lock released + streaming SHA-384 reusable after ICCM hash
  directed_test_iccm_cold_reset_pcr5   PCR5 wiped to zero on cold reset (new journey chain)

Common helpers (acquire_sha_lock, wait_pcr4_ready, run_default_iccm_hash,
sha_ctrl_extend, fw_write_attack, snapshot_pcr, check_pcr_zero/nonzero/match)
are factored into a new shared library libs/iccm_hash/. The existing
directed_test_iccm_hash is refactored to use these helpers without behavior
change. All 7 new tests are added to caliptra_top_nightly_directed_regression.yml,
and CaliptraPreReleaseTestPlan.md is updated: each new test gets a Test
Iterations subsection (matching the existing two), the Test Suite table is
expanded, and the (now empty) Coverage Gaps section is dropped.

(cherry picked from commit abe9323afd3b9a6635eb6a33d4472c37cda580e9)

* [RTL] ICCM write hash measurement: autonomous arming

Remove firmware's responsibility for arming the SHA accelerator that
measures ICCM contents. The accelerator now self-triggers on the first
ICCM write the snoop sees.

* Delete MODE.ICCM_MODE field from sha512_acc_csr (sha512_acc_external_csr.rdl).
  ROM no longer has to write the arming bit before the firmware copy.
* sha512_acc_top.sv now derives iccm_mode autonomously:
  - On the first ICCM write the snoop sees (iccm_hash_dv_i), the live OR
    of iccm_armed and the snoop pulse drives iccm_mode high in the same
    cycle, capturing the first dword without a one-cycle slip.
  - A sticky iccm_armed flop latches on the same trigger (or on
    iccm_lock_i for the zero-length case) so iccm_mode stays high across
    the rest of the firmware copy.
  - iccm_armed is gated by ~iccm_mode_done so writes after PCR4/PCR5
    extend completes do not re-arm, and by ~soc_has_lock so SOC cannot
    suppress the measurement by pre-grabbing the SHA acc lock.
* Add LOCK.LOCK.hwclr and drive it from a new iccm_lock_acquire pulse,
  so HW autonomously claims the SHA acc lock the same cycle iccm_mode
  engages. The existing hwset path still releases the lock after the
  PCR4/PCR5 extend completes.

Coverage:
* Replace the obsolete MODE.ICCM_MODE.hwclr coverpoint with separate
  iccm_armed and iccm_lock_acquire probes/coverpoints in
  soc_ifc_cov_if.sv.

(cherry picked from commit 889e67b550dd02ad4a008257212097a8b9e00530)

* [VAL] ICCM write hash: docs + test updates for autonomous arming

Firmware library and test updates:
* iccm_hash shared library: drop the FW MODE.ICCM_MODE write and
  acquire_sha_lock from run_default_iccm_hash, since HW now arms the
  measurement and claims the SHA acc lock on its own.
* directed_test_iccm_hash, directed_test_iccm_pcr5_journey,
  directed_test_iccm_sha_acc_reuse: drop FW arming and SHA acc lock
  acquire calls; tests now exercise the autonomous flow.
* smoke_test_iccm_hash: same cleanup; firmware just writes the data and
  asserts INTERNAL_ICCM_LOCK. This is the canonical demonstration that
  the hardware engages without any firmware setup.

Test removed:
* directed_test_iccm_mode_write_once is deleted (the MODE.ICCM_MODE bit
  it exercised no longer exists). Removed from the nightly directed
  regression list as well.

New directed test:
* directed_test_iccm_replay_block verifies that once the autonomous
  measurement completes (iccm_mode_done latched), additional ICCM writes
  in the same boot cannot replay or perturb the PCR4/PCR5 values. Runs
  the default ICCM hash, snapshots both PCRs, writes a different pattern
  to ICCM (and re-asserts INTERNAL_ICCM_LOCK as a no-op), then verifies
  PCR4 and PCR5 are byte-for-byte unchanged. Enrolled in
  caliptra_top_nightly_directed_regression.yml.

Docs:
* CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md and CaliptraPreReleaseTestPlan.md
  updated for the autonomous flow and the new replay-block test.

(cherry picked from commit b871910ec6a2e6c588c6b4358c65b493a7de0b6e)

* [RTL] Fix SHA acc LOCK polarity for HW autonomous acquire/release

LOCK.LOCK is 1=locked, 0=free. HW acquire now drives hwset, release
drives hwclr. The acquire pulse is gated on (~iccm_armed &
~iccm_mode_done & ~LOCK.value) so it fires exactly once at the first
ICCM activity and cannot re-fire during the release window. RDL desc,
spec, and testplan updated to match. CSR regen is a no-op (desc text
only).

(cherry picked from commit 0d254a8463fdeda2166e542ed04b1aa203f8def1)

* [RTL] sha512_acc_top: drive iccm_pcr_write_client ports from named signals

Replace assignment-pattern literals on write_ctrl_reg, write_metrics,
and kv_resp with named struct signals assigned in always_comb. Same
struct values, no functional change.

* [RTL] sha512_acc_top: use 'case inside' for extend FSM

- sha512_acc_top: gate notif_cmd_done.hwset with ~iccm_mode so the
  autonomous ICCM hash does not raise an interrupt that firmware never
  requested. Fixes orphan cptra_status_transaction in uvmf_caliptra_top
  mbox_rand_medium_interference scoreboard.
- pv unit TB: tie off unused pv_write/pv_read slots after PV_NUM_WRITE
  bumped to 2; floating X was tripping pv_reg hwif_in isunknown assert
  in pv_l0_regress.
- pv_reg_predictor: drop sha512-map writes to PCR4/PCR5 from the RAL
  mirror so the predicted read value matches the RTL guard in pv.sv
  that blocks pv_write[0] from those entries. Fixes scoreboard read
  mismatches in pv_rand_lock_test and pv_rand_wr_rd_test.

commit_message:
[RTL] Enhance HMAC-512 area/perf (#1274)

* [RTL] Redesign HMAC-512 around single-SHA + LAST

Replace the dual sha512_masked_core architecture (H1 + H2) with a
single time-multiplexed engine. Adds an inner_digest capture register
so the surviving SHA reruns the outer pass over the captured H1 digest.

- hmac_core: 6-state FSM IDLE -> IPAD -> MSG -> OPAD -> HMAC -> DONE
  with a 4-way input mux on sha_block (ipad / msg / opad / hmac_padded);
  is_last_block flag latches LAST at IDLE so MSG knows whether to stop
  or continue to outer; shrink LFSR array from 12 to 6 to match the
  192-bit entropy seed.
- hmac: plumb the LAST command from the wrapper into hmac_core; remove
  the core_is_last_block gating on core_tag_we so tag_valid carries
  its natural meaning again.
- hmac_drbg: advance on rising edge of HMAC_ready instead of
  HMAC_tag_valid_edge so DRBG no longer relies on intermediate-block
  digest_valid pulses.

* [RDL] Add CTRL.LAST; shrink LFSR_SEED 12->6

- hmac_reg.rdl: add LAST field at bit 5 of HMAC512_CTRL; shrink
  LFSR_SEED array from 12 to 6 dwords (192-bit entropy)
- regenerate hmac_reg.sv, hmac_reg_pkg.sv, hmac_reg_uvm.sv
- regenerate integration caliptra_reg.h, caliptra_reg_defines.svh,
  caliptra_reg_field_defines.svh for both passive and subsystem modes

* [RTL] Restore CTRL_ENTROPY state in hmac_core

Bring back the serial CTRL_ENTROPY state that captures a fresh
sha512_masked digest of the entropy_block before IPAD. Remove the
dead `assign lfsr_entropy = lfsr_seed` and restore the full 4-mode
hashing-algorithm comment on mode_reg.

Cost: +178 cy per INIT relative to the previous single-SHA build:
  * +89 cy: dedicated CTRL_ENTROPY SHA call. In the old parallel
    H1+H2 design this entropy hash ran on H2 in parallel with H1's
    IPAD; with one SHA core this hop is now serial.
  * +89 cy: the OPAD hash. In the old design it ran on H2 in parallel
    with H1's message-block hash; on the single SHA core it is now
    serial with MSG (already discussed in prior review).

* [RTL] Drop modifier triggers; refine CTRL.LAST

* hmac.sv: drop last_reg from three gates where it must not appear
  (block_reg_lock release, key_mode_error, key_zero_error). LAST
  cannot start an operation on its own, so only init_reg | next_reg
  qualify as operation-start indicators.
* hmac_reg.rdl: rewrite HMAC512_CTRL.LAST so the field clearly reads
  as a modifier on INIT or NEXT rather than a standalone trigger.

* [VAL] Extend hmac_ctrl_tb for LAST modifier

Update the testbench to match the new HMAC-512 single-SHA control
surface and add semantic coverage for the LAST modifier and the
CTRL_ENTROPY abort path.

CTRL writes that finalize an op now include CTRL_LAST_VALUE (sourced
from HMAC_REG_HMAC512_CTRL_LAST_MASK so we stay aligned with the
regen'd field defines). LFSR seed width drops from 384 to 192 bits to
match the new 6-word LFSR_SEED register, and random_gen() /
write_seed() follow.

New tasks (one call per mode):
- hmac_three_block_test: INIT, NEXT, NEXT|LAST sequence, using the
  RFC 4868 / NIST CAVS HMAC-SHA-384 COUNT=1 vector; the HMAC-SHA-512
  tag is derived from the same key and message.
- last_alone_ignored_test: confirms a bare LAST write cannot start
  the engine and leaves no state behind.
- continuous_cmd_last_test: bombards CTRL with every command variant
  while BUSY and checks the final digest still comes out clean.
- zeroize_mid_op_test: ZEROIZE mid-op drops the engine back to IDLE
  and the next op runs normally.
- init_next_conflict_test: when INIT|NEXT|LAST arrive together, INIT
  wins and NEXT is silently dropped.

* [RTL] Parametrize hmac_core widths for reuse

Promote hardcoded SHA-512 widths in hmac_core to module parameters
so the same core can later be reused for HMAC-256. Defaults match
today's values, so HMAC-512 behavior is unchanged.

BLOCK_SIZE, KEY_SIZE, TAG_SIZE and LFSR_SEED_SIZE are now declared
in hmac_param_pkg and threaded through hmac_core's port widths,
internal signals, IPAD/OPAD pad generation, and the LFSR loop count.
hmac.sv binds these parameters explicitly from its localparams.

SHA-512-specific items (sha512_masked_core, mode_reg, FINAL_PAD and
ENTROPY_PAD literals, inner_digest [511:0]) intentionally remain
hardcoded.

* [RTL] Refactor hmac_core sha_block FSM and params

Address review feedback on hmac_core:

- Drop module parameter block; consume widths from hmac_param_pkg
  (BLOCK_SIZE, KEY_SIZE, TAG_SIZE, LFSR_SEED_SIZE). Add 384
  variant consts (HMAC384_KEY_SIZE/TAG_SIZE/KEY_PAD/TAG_PAD).
- Rename hmac_ctrl_last to hmac_ctrl_ff; it is a flopped copy of
  the command bits, not a "last" command.
- Split sha_block out of state_logic into its own per-state mux
  with default '0.
- Replace hardcoded SHA-512 widths in hmac_core.sv with pkg
  constants (inner_digest slice).
- Move IPAD, OPAD, HMAC384/512_FINAL_PAD and ENTROPY_PAD into the
  pkg; drive the LFSR loop bound from LFSR_SEED_SIZE/32.

Bit-exact for every reachable hmac_ctrl_ff state.

* [RTL] Parametrize hmac_drbg LFSR seed width

Add LFSR_LENGTH parameter (default 192) on hmac_drbg and narrow
the lfsr_seed port from REG_SIZE (384) to LFSR_LENGTH bits to
match the new hmac_core LFSR seed size. Update the standalone
TB widths to follow.

Use 192'(random_gen()) instead of random_gen()[191:0] on the seed
assignments; the part-select on a function-call return is rejected
by VCS R-2020.12-SP2 (and is only marginally legal SV-2017).

* [RTL] Use new pkg widths in hmac.sv and flag LAST-alone

Apply the hmac_param_pkg constants from the previous commit and
add the LAST-without-INIT/NEXT error:

- get_mask now uses HMAC384_TAG_SIZE / HMAC384_TAG_PAD instead of
  literal 15:12 / 511:128.
- key_mode_error key check uses HMAC384_KEY_SIZE/DATA_WIDTH
  instead of literal 128'b0. No HMAC384_*_DWORDS helpers; each
  derived width is used exactly once.
- Flag LAST without INIT or NEXT: edge-detect last_alone_error
  and hw-set error2_sts (sha256 convention: keep generic
  errorN_sts RDL names, semantic meaning lives in the RTL
  signal). Uses *_reg (KV-gated) sources so it cannot false-fire
  during KV-pending stalls; INIT|LAST and NEXT|LAST still work.

last_alone_error is purely combinational and is not folded into
error_flag. This matches sha256: its invalid_sha_op is also a
one-cycle combinational signal that only feeds error1_sts.hwset
and never blocks the engine. The RW1C status bit on the SW side
provides the stickiness firmware needs; the RTL signal stays
non-sticky so a stray LAST does not gate future digest writes.

* [VAL] Parametrize hmac_ctrl_tb and verify LAST error

- Import hmac_param_pkg in the bench and use BLOCK_SIZE,
  KEY_SIZE, TAG_SIZE, HMAC384_KEY_PAD, HMAC384_TAG_PAD in task
  signatures and reg decls. Add hmac_param_pkg.sv to the
  hmac_ctrl_tb compile.yml so the symbols resolve at vlogan.
- Fix HMAC-384 expected-tag padding: was HMAC384_KEY_PAD, should
  be HMAC384_TAG_PAD. Same value today, just the right name.
- Rename last_alone_ignored_test to last_alone_error_test and
  check ERROR2_STS after a LAST without INIT/NEXT to verify the
  new interrupt path. Follow-up valid op confirms the engine
  recovers.

* [CI] Update pr_timestamp and pr_hash stamps

* [RDL] Document KV polling contract for INIT/NEXT

INIT and NEXT pulses are masked when KV is not ready, matching
sha512's convention. Note in the field descriptions that SW must
poll HMAC512_KV_RD_KEY_STATUS.READY and HMAC512_KV_RD_BLOCK_STATUS.READY
before writing the bit, and clarify that STATUS.READY only tracks
the HMAC pipeline, not KV readiness.

No RTL change. Generated reg files do not embed field descriptions,
so no regen is needed.

* [RTL] Pulse tag_valid on intermediate blocks for save/restore prep

After a non-LAST CTRL_MSG block completes, pulse digest_valid before dropping to IDLE. Restores main's per-block tag_valid behavior in the refactored single-SHA hmac_core and exposes intermediate inner-hash H via the existing TAG register for future save/restore.

No new ports or output flags. All hmac.sv consumers (KV write, notif_cmd_done, kv_data_present_reset, dest_data_avail) keep using core_tag_we as in main; the final block overwrites intermediate H in KV.

Revert hmac_drbg edge detector to HMAC_tag_valid_edge/_last (matches main now that tag_valid pulses per block).

Verified: hmac_ctrl_tb, hmac_drbg_tb.

* [UVM] Add HMAC LAST modifier and last-alone test

Align the HMAC UVMF env with the new CTRL.LAST modifier and the
LAST-alone error path added in the HMAC redesign.

Driver BFM: issue INIT|LAST for single-block ops and NEXT|LAST for
the final block of multi-block ops, shrink LFSR_SEED writes from
12 to 6 words, and fix the inner-SHA msg_size to include the
1024-bit K^ipad block. Add a last_alone_error_test task that
issues a LAST-alone CTRL write followed by a legal hmac512 op so
the scoreboard still sees one expected/actual digest pair.

Transaction/interface: add op == 3'b100 (last_alone_op) and expose
last_alone_error_edge on HMAC_in_if for coverage sampling.

Predictor: handle op == 3'b100 by predicting the follow-up hmac512
digest so scoreboard MATCH proves clean recovery after the illegal
write.

Coverage: sample last_reg and the last_alone_error chain, and
replace hmac_cmd_cp with single-pulse bins for init, next,
last_alone_ignored, init_last and next_last so any RTL regression
that drops the detector is caught.

New test: HMAC_last_alone_error_test/_sequence run the BFM task
above and are registered in HMAC sim testlist.yaml and the nightly
random regression yml.

* [RTL] Flag HMAC LAST-alone error and drive LAST in flows

Wire last_alone_error directly from CTRL.LAST/INIT/NEXT bits
(SHA256 invalid_sha_op style) instead of the KV-gated *_reg
copies, so the error fires on every illegal LAST-alone write
regardless of KV state. error2_sts stickiness is preserved via
the existing RDL hwset path.

Update HMAC firmware flows to drive the new CTRL.LAST modifier:
single-block ops issue INIT|LAST, multi-block ops finish with
NEXT|LAST. Touches libs/hmac and consumer smoke tests.

Extend smoke_test_hmac_errortrigger with a stage that writes
LAST alone and confirms hmac_error fires via the ISR path, so
integration regression catches any regression dropping the new
detector.

* [RTL] Use LFSR_SEED_SIZE from hmac_param_pkg in ecc DRBG iface

* [RTL] Drop redundant hmac_param_pkg.sv from hmac_ctrl_tb target

hmac_ctrl_tb already requires hmac_ctrl, whose rtl target lists
hmac_param_pkg.sv. Re-listing it in the tb target was redundant
and forced the ADO promote pipeline's FILE LIST CHECK to regenerate
all ~99 .vf file lists.

* [VAL] update kv_boot_flow LFSR_SEED loop bound for 6-word seed

The HMAC512 LFSR_SEED register was shrunk from 12 dwords to 6 dwords
in the single-SHA redesign. kv_boot_flow.c still referenced the old
LFSR_SEED_11 constant, breaking the smoke_test_kv_boot_flow_monitor
compile on the L0 regression. Update the loop upper bound to
LFSR_SEED_5 to match the new register layout.

commit_message:
[RTL] Key vault monitor and enforcement (#1260)

* fixes kv crypto flow tests so that they don't pick KV slot 23 and hang the DOE

* Add boot flow transition enforcement for DICE key integrity

   Add hardware-enforced monitoring and access control for key vault slots
   across ROM->FMC->RT boot phase transitions.

   Boot flow monitor (caliptra_top.sv):
   - Detect transitions via ICCM bank read address matching
   - MuBi4-encoded signals for glitch resistance
   - Error on fetch without lock, out-of-order transition, or invalid state

   KV monitor and enforcement (kv.sv):
   - Validate dest_valid on DICE slots at each transition
   - Per-slot saturating write counters detect truncated derivation chains
   - HW-driven lock_wr/lock_use (hwset) per boot phase
   - Atomic slot clearing of unreferenced keys at transitions
   - Alert flushes all entries via CPTRA_HW_ERROR_FATAL.kv_error

   ICCM region shadow registers (soc_ifc_top.sv, soc_ifc_internal_reg.rdl):
   - 4 registers backed by caliptra_prim_subreg_shadow
   - 2-phase write protocol, phase-clear-on-read, error lockout
   - shadow_storage_err (FATAL[5]), shadow_update_err (NON_FATAL[3])

   DOE lockdown (doe_cbc.sv): Clear DOE_CTRL.CMD once FMC/RT active

   SVA (kv_boot_flow_sva.sv): 30 assertions for enforcement correctness

   Docs: Feature spec in CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md (Pre-release)

* Add tests and test plan for boot flow transition enforcement

   Add 4 directed/smoke tests for KV boot flow enforcement feature:
   - smoke/kv_boot_flow_monitor: Happy-path DICE derivation + transitions
   - directed/kv_enforcement: lock_wr, lock_use, DOE lockdown, ROM callback
   - directed/kv_iccm_region: Shadow register programming, lock, reset, errors
   - directed/kv_monitor_neg: dest_valid and write count fault injection

   Register tests in L0 (smoke) and nightly directed regression YAMLs.
   Add TB service for boot_flow_monitor_en force/release.
   Create docs/CaliptraPreReleaseTestPlan.md with test cases, SVA summary,
   covergroup plan, and coverage gaps.

* cover groups for kv enfrocement and boot flow monitor feature

document shadow register description in rdl

index 00000000..1029a9e9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/integration/rtl/boot_flow_monitor.sv
@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@

+// See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+// limitations under the License.
+//
+// Boot Flow Monitor
+// Monitors ICCM fetch activity to detect ROM->FMC and FMC->RT transitions.
+// Outputs mubi4 signals consumed by the keyvault enforcement logic.
+
+module boot_flow_monitor
+    import caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg::*;
+    import el2_pkg::*;
+    #(
+    `include "el2_param.vh"
+    )
+    (
+        input logic clk,
+        input logic cptra_uc_rst_b,
+
+        // ICCM memory interface (from el2_mem_export)
+        input logic [pt.ICCM_NUM_BANKS-1:0]                                        iccm_clken,
+        input logic [pt.ICCM_NUM_BANKS-1:0]                                        iccm_wren_bank,
+        input logic [pt.ICCM_NUM_BANKS-1:0][pt.ICCM_BITS-1:pt.ICCM_BANK_INDEX_LO]  iccm_addr_bank,
+
+        // Region bounds (from shadow registers)
+        input logic [pt.ICCM_BITS-1:0] iccm_fmc_start_addr,
+        input logic [pt.ICCM_BITS-1:0] iccm_fmc_end_addr,
+        input logic [pt.ICCM_BITS-1:0] iccm_rt_start_addr,
+        input logic [pt.ICCM_BITS-1:0] iccm_rt_end_addr,
+
+        // Control
+        input logic iccm_region_lock,
+        input logic boot_flow_monitor_en,
+        input logic fw_update_rst_window,
+
+        // Outputs
+        output mubi4_t boot_flow_fmc_o,
+        output mubi4_t boot_flow_rt_o,
+        output mubi4_t boot_flow_error_o
+    );
+
+    // Internal signals
+    logic [pt.ICCM_NUM_BANKS-1:0]                   iccm_read_en;
+    logic [pt.ICCM_NUM_BANKS-1:0][pt.ICCM_BITS-1:0] iccm_read_addr;
+    logic iccm_read_fmc;
+    logic iccm_read_rt;
+    logic iccm_read_any;
+
+    mubi4_t boot_flow_fmc_q;
+    mubi4_t boot_flow_rt_q;
+    mubi4_t boot_flow_error_q;
+
+    // ICCM fetch region detection
+    // Reconstruct full byte address from per-bank row address + bank index.
+    // The bank index occupies bits [ICCM_BANK_INDEX_LO-1 : ICCM_BANK_INDEX_LO-ICCM_BANK_BITS]
+    // and the row address sits above that. The low bits below the bank index
+    // are zero-filled since ICCM is word-aligned. Region start/end addresses
+    // programmed via soc_ifc must be aligned to the bank interleave granularity
+    // (2^ICCM_BANK_INDEX_LO bytes) for correct matching.
+    //
+    // Note: iccm_clken includes clk_override (VeeR MCGC CSR bit 0) which forces
+    // bank clocks on without an actual read/write. Caliptra FW never writes MCGC,
+    // and boot_flow_monitor_en is deasserted in scan mode (where clk_override may
+    // be set), so false read detection from clk_override is not possible in
+    // normal operation.
+    always_comb begin
+        iccm_read_fmc = '0;
+        iccm_read_rt  = '0;
+        iccm_read_any = '0;
+        for (int bank = 0; bank < pt.ICCM_NUM_BANKS; bank++) begin
+            iccm_read_en[bank] = iccm_clken[bank] && ~iccm_wren_bank[bank];
+            iccm_read_addr[bank] = {iccm_addr_bank[bank], pt.ICCM_BANK_BITS'(bank), {(pt.ICCM_BANK_INDEX_LO - pt.ICCM_BANK_BITS){1'b0}}};
+
+            iccm_read_fmc |= iccm_read_en[bank] && (iccm_read_addr[bank] inside {[iccm_fmc_start_addr:iccm_fmc_end_addr]});
+            iccm_read_rt  |= iccm_read_en[bank] && (iccm_read_addr[bank] inside {[iccm_rt_start_addr:iccm_rt_end_addr]});
+            iccm_read_any |= iccm_read_en[bank];
+        end
+    end
+
+    // Boot flow state machine
+    // Synchronous soft-reset via fw_update_rst_window clears boot_flow flops cleanly
+    // on posedge clk before cptra_uc_rst_b deasserts. This eliminates RDC metastability
+    // from the async reset path into the cptra_noncore_rst_b domain.
+    always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge cptra_uc_rst_b) begin
+        if (!cptra_uc_rst_b) begin
+            boot_flow_fmc_q   <= MuBi4False;
+            boot_flow_rt_q    <= MuBi4False;
+            boot_flow_error_q <= MuBi4False;
+        end else if (fw_update_rst_window) begin
+            boot_flow_fmc_q   <= MuBi4False;
+            boot_flow_rt_q    <= MuBi4False;
+            boot_flow_error_q <= MuBi4False;
+        end else if (boot_flow_monitor_en) begin
+            // Transition from ROM to FMC: first fetch from FMC region after lock
+            if (iccm_region_lock && mubi4_test_false_strict(boot_flow_fmc_q) && iccm_read_fmc) begin
+                boot_flow_fmc_q <= MuBi4True;
+            end
+
+            // Transition from FMC to RT: first fetch from RT region after lock
+            // Gated on boot_flow_fmc_q -- an RT fetch without FMC entered is an error,
+            // not a valid transition. This prevents a transient enter_rt pulse that could
+            // trigger KV enforcement before the error is raised.
+            if (iccm_region_lock && mubi4_test_true_strict(boot_flow_fmc_q) &&
+                mubi4_test_false_strict(boot_flow_rt_q) && iccm_read_rt) begin
+                boot_flow_rt_q <= MuBi4True;
+            end
+
+            // Error conditions:
+            //   1. Any ICCM fetch before region lock is set
+            //   2. RT region fetch without FMC entered (illegal ROM->RT jump)
+            //   3. ICCM fetch outside both FMC and RT regions after lock
+            //   4. MuBi integrity check on FSM state flops
+            boot_flow_error_q <= (iccm_read_any && !iccm_region_lock) ||
+                                 (iccm_read_rt && mubi4_test_false_strict(boot_flow_fmc_q)) ||
+                                 (iccm_region_lock && iccm_read_any && !iccm_read_fmc && !iccm_read_rt) ||
+                                 mubi4_test_invalid(boot_flow_fmc_q) || mubi4_test_invalid(boot_flow_rt_q) || mubi4_test_invalid(boot_flow_error_q)
+                                 ? MuBi4True : boot_flow_error_q;
+        end
+    end
+
+    assign boot_flow_fmc_o   = boot_flow_fmc_q;
+    assign boot_flow_rt_o    = boot_flow_rt_q;
+    assign boot_flow_error_o = boot_flow_error_q;
+
+endmodule

+  // ============================================================

+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: doe_cmd_lock not asserted during FMC phase");
+
+  DoeCmdLockInRt_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n || !monitor_en)
+    rt_true |-> doe_cmd_lock
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: doe_cmd_lock not asserted during RT phase");
+
+  // ============================================================
+  // Section 8: Write Counters
+  // What: Counters increment on crypto engine writes, not on SW clear
+  // Why: Detects truncated DICE derivation chains
+  // ============================================================
+
+  // Write counter increments on qualified crypto write, not on flush or clear
+  WriteCountFmcCdiIncr_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (crypto_wr_fmc_cdi && write_count_fmc_cdi < 3'd7 && !flush_keyvault) |=> (write_count_fmc_cdi == $past(write_count_fmc_cdi) + 3'd1)
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_cdi did not increment on crypto write");
+
+  WriteCountFmcEcdsaIncr_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (crypto_wr_fmc_ecdsa && write_count_fmc_ecdsa < 3'd7 && !flush_keyvault) |=> (write_count_fmc_ecdsa == $past(write_count_fmc_ecdsa) + 3'd1)
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_ecdsa did not increment on crypto write");
+
+  WriteCountFmcMldsaIncr_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (crypto_wr_fmc_mldsa && write_count_fmc_mldsa < 3'd7 && !flush_keyvault) |=> (write_count_fmc_mldsa == $past(write_count_fmc_mldsa) + 3'd1)
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_mldsa did not increment on crypto write");
+
+  // What: Counters saturate at 7 (3'b111), never wrap -- unless cleared by flush
+  WriteCountFmcCdiSaturate_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (write_count_fmc_cdi == 3'd7 && !flush_keyvault) |=> (write_count_fmc_cdi == 3'd7)
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_cdi wrapped past saturation");
+
+  WriteCountFmcEcdsaSaturate_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (write_count_fmc_ecdsa == 3'd7 && !flush_keyvault) |=> (write_count_fmc_ecdsa == 3'd7)
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_ecdsa wrapped past saturation");
+
+  WriteCountFmcMldsaSaturate_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (write_count_fmc_mldsa == 3'd7 && !flush_keyvault) |=> (write_count_fmc_mldsa == 3'd7)
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_mldsa wrapped past saturation");
+
+  // What: Counters must not increment when the slot is locked (lock_wr or lock_use)
+  // Why: lock_wr/lock_use gates key_entry_we, so crypto_wr_* stays 0 on locked slots
+  WriteCountFmcCdiStableLocked_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    ((lock_wr_q[KV_SLOT_FMC_CDI] | lock_use_q[KV_SLOT_FMC_CDI]) && !flush_keyvault) |=>

+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_cdi changed while slot locked");
+
+  WriteCountFmcEcdsaStableLocked_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    ((lock_wr_q[KV_SLOT_FMC_ECDSA] | lock_use_q[KV_SLOT_FMC_ECDSA]) && !flush_keyvault) |=>
+      (write_count_fmc_ecdsa == $past(write_count_fmc_ecdsa))
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_ecdsa changed while slot locked");
+
+  WriteCountFmcMldsaStableLocked_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    ((lock_wr_q[KV_SLOT_FMC_MLDSA] | lock_use_q[KV_SLOT_FMC_MLDSA]) && !flush_keyvault) |=>
+      (write_count_fmc_mldsa == $past(write_count_fmc_mldsa))
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_mldsa changed while slot locked");
+
+  // What: Counters must not increment when key_entry_clear is active on the slot
+  // Why: crypto_wr_* is explicitly gated by ~key_entry_clear to prevent counting clear ops
+  WriteCountFmcCdiStableClear_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (key_entry_clear[KV_SLOT_FMC_CDI] && !flush_keyvault) |=>
+      (write_count_fmc_cdi == $past(write_count_fmc_cdi))
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_cdi changed during key_entry_clear");
+
+  WriteCountFmcEcdsaStableClear_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (key_entry_clear[KV_SLOT_FMC_ECDSA] && !flush_keyvault) |=>
+      (write_count_fmc_ecdsa == $past(write_count_fmc_ecdsa))
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_ecdsa changed during key_entry_clear");
+
+  WriteCountFmcMldsaStableClear_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    (key_entry_clear[KV_SLOT_FMC_MLDSA] && !flush_keyvault) |=>
+      (write_count_fmc_mldsa == $past(write_count_fmc_mldsa))
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_mldsa changed during key_entry_clear");

+  // Why: Hard reset clears everything; flush/debug unlock invalidates keys so counters restart

+    @(posedge clk)
+    !`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood |-> (write_count_fmc_cdi == 3'd0)
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_cdi not zero during hard reset");
+
+  WriteCountFmcEcdsaHardReset_A: assert property (

+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: write_count_fmc_ecdsa not zero during hard reset");
+
+  WriteCountFmcMldsaHardReset_A: assert property (

+  // Section 9: ICCM Region Register Properties
+  // ============================================================

+  // What: boot_flow_error fires if any ICCM fetch occurs while ICCM_REGION_LOCK = 0
+  // Why: Unprogrammed regions must not be trusted
+  IccmFetchWithoutLock_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!core_rst_n || !monitor_en)

+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!core_rst_n)

+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: ICCM_REGION_LOCK cleared without reset");
+
+  // What: All 4 address registers and ICCM_REGION_LOCK reset to 0 on cptra_noncore_rst_b
+  // Why: ROM must reprogram regions on every boot cycle
+  // Note: Uses noncore_rst_n because the shadow registers and ICCM_REGION_LOCK
+  //       in soc_ifc_top use cptra_noncore_rst_b (they survive warm resets).
+  IccmRegionLockReset_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk)
+    !noncore_rst_n |-> !iccm_region_lock
+  ) else $display("SVA ERROR: ICCM_REGION_LOCK not zero during noncore reset");

+  // Section 10: Cover Properties
+  // ============================================================

+  );
+
+  // Cover: boot_flow_error fires on unlocked ICCM fetch

+  );
+
+  // Cover: Stable owner key preserved at enter_fmc
+  StableOwnerPreservedAtFmc_C: cover property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!core_rst_n || !monitor_en)

+
+  // Cover: OCP Lock slots preserved at enter_fmc
+  OcpLockMdkPreservedAtFmc_C: cover property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!core_rst_n || !monitor_en)
+    enter_fmc && ocp_lock_mode_en && !boot_flow_key_clear[OCP_LOCK_RT_OBF_KEY_KV_SLOT]
+  );
+
+  OcpLockHekPreservedAtFmc_C: cover property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!core_rst_n || !monitor_en)
+    enter_fmc && ocp_lock_mode_en && !boot_flow_key_clear[OCP_LOCK_HEK_SEED_KV_SLOT]
+  );
+
+  // ============================================================
+  // Section 7: Write counter clearing on flush
+  // What: After flush_keyvault, all write counters must be zero
+  // Why: Prevents stale counter values from masking a truncated
+  //      DICE derivation after debug unlock or scan mode entry
+  // Timing: 1 cycle -- counters are in an always_ff with flush as sync clear
+  // ============================================================
+
+  WriteCountClearOnFlush_Cdi_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    flush_keyvault |=> (write_count_fmc_cdi == '0)
+  ) else $display("SVA FAIL: write_count_fmc_cdi not cleared after flush");
+
+  WriteCountClearOnFlush_Ecdsa_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    flush_keyvault |=> (write_count_fmc_ecdsa == '0)
+  ) else $display("SVA FAIL: write_count_fmc_ecdsa not cleared after flush");
+
+  WriteCountClearOnFlush_Mldsa_A: assert property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    flush_keyvault |=> (write_count_fmc_mldsa == '0)
+  ) else $display("SVA FAIL: write_count_fmc_mldsa not cleared after flush");
+
+  // Cover: flush_keyvault fires with non-zero counters
+  FlushWithNonZeroCounters_C: cover property (
+    @(posedge clk) disable iff (!`KV_PATH.cptra_pwrgood)
+    flush_keyvault && (write_count_fmc_cdi != '0)
+  );
+
+endmodule
